title: Ride Sharing Platform: Complete Architecture
description: Design a ride sharing platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a ride sharing platform that connects riders with nearby drivers in real time. Riders request rides from their current location, the system matches them with the best available driver within seconds, tracks the trip with live GPS updates, calculates dynamic fares including surge pricing, and processes payments after the ride ends. The platform must also support driver dispatch, trip history, ratings, and emergency SOS features.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Riders request rides with pickup and drop-off locations via map or text
Drivers go online, accept ride requests, and navigate to pickup
Real-time GPS tracking updates rider and driver apps every 2-5 seconds
Matching engine selects the nearest driver within 30 seconds
Calculate ETA from driver to pickup and pickup to destination using map data
Apply dynamic surge pricing based on local demand and driver supply
Track trip status: requested, matched, arriving, in-progress, completed, canceled
Process payment after trip completion using saved payment methods
Allow riders and drivers to rate each other after trip completion
Trigger SOS alerts to emergency contacts and ops when activated

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: 99.5% availability for dispatch and matching services
Sub-2-second matching time from ride request to driver acceptance
Support 10,000+ concurrent drivers per city with location updates
GPS updates delivered to drivers within 2 seconds of rider movement
Geospatial queries for nearest driver complete in under 200ms
Surge pricing calculations update every 60 seconds per zone
Trip history and receipts available within 5 minutes of completion
SOS alert reaches ops and emergency contacts within 1 second

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application that handles rider requests, driver dispatch, GPS tracking, fare calculation, payment processing, and ratings. Use Azure SQL or AWS RDS for relational data. WebSockets handle real-time location updates between drivers and the dispatch server. The monolith lets you validate the core matching and GPS pipeline before scaling to microservices.

data.text: At scale, split into microservices to handle high-frequency location updates and geospatial matching independently. Dispatch Service receives ride requests. Matching Engine runs geospatial queries to find the nearest available driver. Location Service ingests GPS pings and publishes driver positions. Trip Service manages the ride lifecycle. Pricing Service calculates fares and surge. Notification Service pushes ride updates via WebSockets. SOS Service handles emergency alerts.

items: Dispatch Service: Receives ride requests, validates pickup and drop-off locations, and emits MatchRequest events to the matching engine.
Matching Engine: Runs geospatial queries against driver locations, applies ETA and driver-rating heuristics, and assigns the best driver within the SLA.
Location Service: Ingests high-frequency GPS pings from drivers via WebSocket or MQTT, stores recent positions in Redis geospatial indexes, and publishes position updates.
Trip Service: Manages the full ride lifecycle from request to completion, handles cancellations, and stores trip legs and route data.
Pricing Service: Calculates base fare, distance, time, and dynamic surge multipliers by geo-zone; exposes fare estimates to rider and driver apps.
Notification Service: Pushes ride status updates, driver arrival alerts, and SOS notifications via WebSocket, FCM, or APNs.

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: A Ride Sharing Platform system requires both simple and scalable designs
Monolith is fastest to validate; microservices are for scale
React + ASP.NET Core provides a robust full-stack foundation
Azure Cosmos DB and Amazon DynamoDB are strong choices for distributed data
Always design for failure: retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks
data.takeaway: Ride Sharing Platform is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
